business_problem: Lidingö stad needed to reduce the manual effort required to review official documents, redact sensitive information and comply with Sweden’s transparency laws without exposing personal or classified data.
solution_summary: As part of the Rätt till insyn project, Lidingö stad worked with IBM and ATEA to test whether generative AI could speed up the confidentiality review process for public-document requests. The municipality’s staff had been manually reading requested documents, identifying personally identifiable or otherwise sensitive information and then redacting material before release. IBM watsonx.ai became the core of the pilot, providing a generative AI layer for analyzing document content and highlighting information that may need redaction. The approach fits into the municipality’s existing document-handling workflow rather than replacing it outright: staff still perform confidentiality assessments, but they do so with machine assistance that shortens review time and improves consistency. The result is a document-processing pattern geared to transparency, privacy and legally compliant public access.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Analyzes official documents to help identify sensitive content that may need redaction before public release.

data_flow: Official documents requested under transparency rules are reviewed with watsonx.ai assistance so staff can identify sensitive content, apply redactions and release compliant versions more quickly.
business_outcome: The municipalities in the project reduced processing time for public-document requests while preserving transparency obligations and better protecting sensitive information.
architecture_clues: Solution supports confidentiality assessments before release
Designed to align with Sweden’s Freedom of the Press Act
evidence_quotes: Lidingö stad Municipality ... uses generative AI to successfully streamline its data masking process, protecting sensitive data, improving efficiency, and ensuring compliance with Sweden’s transparency laws.
